extracted.intended_audience: corporate counsel, investor_relations, compliance officers, and public company executives
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for public companies on complying with SEC Regulation FD when material information is disclosed via social media or third parties, including how to treat non-intentional disclosures and how to use social channels as official disclosure mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt public disclosure requirement under Regulation FD
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation FD requires public companies to promptly make public disclosure of any material information that is unintentionally disclosed to certain categories of persons, including to shareholders under circumstances where it is reasonably foreseeable that such shareholders will transact in the company’s securities on the basis of such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If material information is selectively disclosed (even unintentionally), the company must promptly disclose that information to the public so that all investors have access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing deadline for non-intentional selective disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a non-intentional selective disclosure, Regulation FD requires the company to make a public disclosure of the information as soon as reasonably practicable (but in no event after the later of 24 hours or the commencement of the next day’s trading on the New York Stock Exchange) after learning of the non-intentional disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Companies must act quickly after learning of a non-intentional selective disclosure — at minimum within the 24-hour/next-trading-day backstop — when assessing remedial disclosure steps (press release, Form 8‑K, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes 'public disclosure' for Regulation FD
rubrics_metrics.description: Public disclosure can include issuing a press release or filing a Form 8‑K to disclose the information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When remedying a selective disclosure, use clear, widely-accessible mechanisms (press release, Form 8‑K) to ensure information reaches the market; relying on private channels or obscure posts is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and designation of social media accounts as disclosure channels
rubrics_metrics.description: If companies wish to announce key information via social media accounts, whether the company’s own or those of their executives, such announcements will not meet the 'public disclosure' requirement of Regulation FD unless the company has first adequately informed investors about which social media accounts will be used to disseminate such information and there is evidence that investors look to those accounts as a mechanism to obtain material information about the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formally designate which corporate or executive accounts are official disclosure channels and give advance notice to investors if those accounts will be used for material announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor reliance / evidence that investors use the channel
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements via social media will meet the public disclosure requirement only if there is evidence that investors look to those accounts as a mechanism to obtain material information about the company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before relying on a social channel for disclosure, companies should be able to demonstrate investor followership/subscription/usage or take steps (e.g., cross-promotion, subscription mechanisms) to build that reliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of personal social media accounts of employees/executives
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal social media sites of individuals employed by a public company would not ordinarily be assumed by investors to be channels through which a company would publicly disclose material corporate information, absent advance notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume executive personal accounts qualify as official disclosure channels; if you intend to use them, provide advance notice and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to promptly disclose to all investors after selective disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Even in the case of a non-intentional disclosure to some investors, the company must promptly disclose the key information to all investors within the time period required by Regulation FD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selective dissemination (e.g., post seen by some followers) triggers an obligation to cure via public disclosure that reaches the entire market within the Regulation FD timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate which social media channels are useful for investor communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Companies should evaluate which social media channels may be useful to communicate information to investors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should consider investor behavior, channel reach, and the channel’s suitability for timely, verifiable dissemination of material information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide investors opportunities to subscribe/follow/join disclosure channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide investors and other market participants opportunities to subscribe, follow, or join such channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it simple for investors to opt into official channels (follow links on IR site, sign-up forms) to help establish those channels as relied-upon sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alert investors and the market about use of chosen social channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Alert investors and the markets of the use of such channels to disseminate material company information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use press releases, website notices, Form 8‑K filings, and investor-relations communications to notify the market which social accounts will be used for material disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual-release (simultaneous Regulation FD-compliant release) until reliance established
rubrics_metrics.description: Until there is evidence that investors use the relevant social media channel to obtain information about the company, consider also simultaneously releasing any material information in another Regulation FD‑compliant manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When making material announcements on social media, also issue a press release or file a Form 8‑K at the same time unless investor reliance on the social channel has been established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies and procedures for third-party posting on behalf of company/personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider creating policies or procedures outlining the 'rules of the road' if third parties are permitted to post information on behalf of the company and its personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish authorization, review, and escalation procedures for third-party or PR firm posts; limit posting privileges and require clearance for material content to avoid unintentional selective disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk of enforcement and penalties for non-intentional disclosures by third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: The SEC treated a post by a third‑party public relations firm on the CEO’s personal social accounts as a 'non‑intentional' disclosure and required DraftKings to pay a $200,000 penalty for failing to promptly disseminate the material non‑public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that authorized third parties posting material information on executive accounts can trigger Regulation FD enforcement if the company fails to timely cure the selective disclosure; maintain controls and remedial plans.
